title: Demolition Starts with a Plan: Steel Structure Collapse
summary: A laborer with no demolition experience was crushed and killed when a 30-foot steel structure collapsed in a different direction than the crew planned. Survey the structure, write a plan, and make sure everyone knows it before cutting.
talking_points: A crew was taking down a 30-foot steel structure to sell as scrap. It sat on sloping pavement, and its legs were different lengths, so it leaned about four feet downhill.

The crew cut it with a torch from a forklift platform and rigged a rope to pull it in the direction of the lean. While the laborer cut a cross brace from a stepladder, the structure collapsed the opposite way and a steel beam crushed him. He had never done demolition work.

Before demolition starts, a competent person must make an engineering survey of the structure. It checks the structure's strength and the chance of unplanned collapse of any part. Keep the written proof.
Demolition must be done under competent supervision with safe working conditions for workers.
Write a project-specific demolition safety plan with step-by-step instructions for how the work will be done safely.
Tell every worker what the plan says and what hazards and precautions apply to them.
site_hazards_to_check: A structure on slope, uneven ground, or with legs of different lengths
Unplanned fall direction or no plan for how members will come down
Workers cutting from stepladders or temporary platforms near load-bearing parts
New or inexperienced workers on demolition tasks without training
People standing in the possible fall zone
discussion_questions: Has a competent person surveyed this structure, and where is the written survey?
What is the planned fall direction, and what if it does not go that way?
Who has not yet been briefed on the demolition plan?
